Game is great after all these years, although a lot of bugs are still present, but mods are sure to fix it tho. Multiplayer is still alive and kicking and the use of a mod manager (console commands) will fix the grinding issue, Bioware doesn't care about hacking or cheating anymore but that's up to you if you wanna do that stuff. Also a FOV slider is a must and there is talk of a mod that will add a FOV slider into the game soon.

Over all, pretty good game, would bang Liara's blue ass again

good multiplayer

There's a few problems with this game. 

1) EA is part of this social trend to over-represent women in entertainment. Aria, EDI, Liara, etc... 
2) EA is heavily promoting homosexuality.  Seriously, this is excessive. 
3) The gameplay is often lacking. The AI is severely sub-par and underwhelming, and often there's simply no enemies when there probably should be.

Because of this, the storyline and gameplay are lacking. 5/10

I was going to wait to write a review because I plan on playing Mass Effect Legendary Edition and was going to write a review for the series as a whole there, but there are a few things I just want to say anyways right now after having completing Mass Effect 3 a few days ago and letting everything sink in. 

I can say without a doubt that the Mass Effect series is the most unique story telling experience I've ever played. The amount of impact your choices actually make and every single little detail that they can change to the ending of each game is actually mind-blowing. Not to mention the story line and atmosphere of the games themselves just really struck me hard. I loved the idea of space growing up and the Mass Effect universe really brought home the memories of what I imagined some parts of the universe might actually be like one day. 

Despite the actually large amount of characters and squadmates you meet throughout the series, each and every one I felt like I was able to make a connection with, and the beauty about this series is that you don't even have to bond with certain characters if you don't want to, that's your choice. I personally played most, if not all, the character/squadmate specifc quests but even those are optional should you not want to play them, or could even be missable depending on choices made prior, because that's also another thing, your choices carry across each game, which again just completely impressed me from the people in charge of the story development. Your choices in all the games, but especially in Mass Effect 2 and 3, quite literally decides who lives and who dies, and some of them aren't even obvious until the consequences of an action made a while ago occurs and you think back and go, "oh". 

I will save the rest of my thoughts for the series when I eventually play legendary edition, but will go more into detail of why Mass Effect 3 is my favorite of the trilogy. 

Right from the start of the game, the story drew me in and got me invested for the endgame, I truly felt Commander Shepard's determination and drive for the final fight against the Reapers. Although this endgame took time and effort (depending on how much of the side content and equipment you worked to gain), I got to reconnect with previous characters and connect with new ones. I really enjoyed all of the DLCs that were included, especially the Citadel DLC, because I feel like the player gets a chance to take a break from the chaos of the main story and actually gets to take time to just focus on connecting with characters/squadmates, new and old, one last time before reaching the endgame. 

I also liked the gameplay system for mass effect, and Mass Effect 3 was my favorite. The only small problem I encountered playing on a keyboard and mouse was that the cover system would get kinda wonky for me sometimes, more specifically trying to move out of cover when the game auto-detected other cover options and moved me to those instead when I didn't want to. Like all three games, I also really appreciated the unique dialogue from each squadmate during missions depending on who you decided to take with you. 

And then there is the soundtrack. As I have said in many of my reviews, the soundtrack is a large part of what makes a videogame for me, whether it is immersing me in the moment or just a bop to listen to, and Mass Effect 3's soundtrack out of all the games in the trilogy hit me the hardest and actually made me emotional at the end of the journey. The reprise of the Earth's destruction track (at the beginning of ME3) that plays in "An End, Once And For All" at the ending sequence for Mass Effect 3 hit hardest, and actually made me sit back and think of how far Shepard and his team had come to get to the end point, while the ending played out. On a side note, it genuinely makes me want to learn how to play the piano now, just so I can play that track. 

The best part of all of this is that if you wanted to, you could just replay the entire series and create a whole different path for Shepard and his team. My playthrough of the original mass effect games wasn't perfect, which is why I plan on replaying them in the Legendary Edition to get the absolute best endings or outcomes for Shepard and everyone on his squad. 

That is all I have to say for now. Again, I was planning on waiting until finishing Legendary Edition to write a review, but after finishing this game I just had to get some of the things I was thinking out there.

Mass Effect will truly be one of the most memorable and favorite experiences of mine.
